page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, full width. No marginal notes. Page number at the head, running head below it, catchword at the foot right.

main_text.p: anno Chrifti 1700: confulendum eft calendairiuffi Arabicum, in quo retulimus, ante æram Muhammeda-nam à Nabonafaro elapfos fuiffe 499802 dies: qui fi fubtrahantur ab annis Nabonafari 2448, hoc eft, à diebus in vniuerfum 893520, qui à Nabonafaro vfque ad 24 lunij, currentis anni Chrifti 1700 funt praeteriti; remanent 593718 dies, quod eft interuallum inter æram Hegiræ Muhamedanam, & inter 24 diem lunij, labente anno Chrifti 1700. Iftud interuallum, quod copleditur dies 593718, fi diuidatur per 11063 1 [?] dies, fuppeditat cyclos Arabicos triginta feptem, hoc eft, annos Arabicos mille centum & decem, & fuperfunt 371 dies, qui conflant annum vnum Arabicum, & remanent feptendecim dies. Annus ille fi ad datur ad annos mille centum & decem, conflatur fumma mille centum & vndecim annorum Arabicorum, qui praeterierunt ad tempus nominatum: cum autem fimul elapfi fuerint 17 dies, manifeste apparet dies illos feptendecim pertinere ad menfem Muharam, currentis anni Hagareni millefimi centefimi & duodecimi, hoc eft, anni fecundi in cyclo triacontaeterico Arabum trigefimo octauo. Colligitur itaque diem 24 lunij iuxta ftilum veterem, currente anno Chrifti 1700, refpondere diei decimo octauo menfis Muharam, labente anno Hagareno 1112: & fimul percipitur neomeniam Muharam anni prædicti Hagareni, incidere in diem feptimum lunij, feriam fextam, in quam etiam incurrit neomenia Tamuz anni Iudaici 5460. Sane annus Chrifti 1700 numerum aureum habet X, qui in tabella Nicaena ponitur ad diem 14 Martij, & recurrit die vndecimo lunij, vbi falfum nouilunium oftendit iuxta ftilum veterem: fi vero anticipatio lunaris, quæ in diem quintum præ-

page.notes: The page number "126" is printed in an old figure form, read as 126 with some doubt. The numerals in "per 11063 1" (the string after "per") are hard to read; the value 110631 is uncertain and marked [?]. The catchword "ceden-" is partly cut off at the right edge and is read with some doubt. The text is continued on the next page (præ-ceden-).
